approachQuestion.prompt:
Best fixed-width shift. Return the largest sum among all contiguous intervals of exactly w entries. Signed values are allowed; return only that sum.

Input: a=[-3,5,-2,4], w=2. Output: 3.

Constraints: 1 ≤ w ≤ n ≤ 200000; -1000000 ≤ a[i] ≤ 1000000; sums fit signed 64 bits. Prefer the least auxiliary space among methods that scan the data only a constant number of times.

Which approach handles the complete task correctly and efficiently?

options.text: Sum the first w values and initialize best to that sum. Move right one position at a time by subtracting the departing value and adding the arriving value, updating best.
options.feedback: Consecutive windows of the same width differ by exactly one departure and one arrival, regardless of value signs.

options.text: Initialize best to zero, then apply the same moving-window updates.
options.feedback: For [-4,-2], w=1, all legal sums are negative. Returning zero invents an empty window.

options.text: For every possible start sum its w entries from scratch.
options.feedback: This gives correct results, but repeatedly traverses overlapping candidates. The selected summary reuses their shared work.

feedback.reason: Sum the first w values and initialize best to that sum. Move right one position at a time by subtracting the departing value and adding the arriving value, updating best.
details: Sum the first w values and initialize best to that sum. Move right one position at a time by subtracting the departing value and adding the arriving value, updating best.

A fixed width permits subtracting the departing value and adding the arriving one even for signed values. Initialize from the first real window; zero is not a valid default maximum for all-negative input.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the method in the reveal. Choose its tightest worst-case time and worst-case auxiliary-space pair. Use constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

feedback.reason: One initial width-w sum is followed by constant-work shifts.
details: First sum w entries and then update n-w windows. Only current, best and indices are stored. A cumulative array also has linear time but uses removable O(n) storage.
Use constant-time 64-bit arithmetic. Exclude read-only input and required output; include every described table. All loops are iterative, with no recursive stack or input copies.

The first window takes w additions; the remaining n-w shifts each subtract one outgoing value and add one incoming value. Thus w+(n-w)=O(n) total work. O(nw) would rebuild every window sum from scratch. O(w) counts only the first window and omits the subsequent n-w shifts.

Only current sum, best sum, and fixed indices are retained, giving O(1) auxiliary space. The O(n)-space option would count a prefix or per-window sum array that this fixed rolling implementation never allocates. Read-only values and the returned scalar maximum are excluded.
